title: CAEM-001 · OUTPUT 06 — MANDATE CORPUS
$why_this_exists: CAEM-001 §1 mapped THIRTEEN mandated concepts to canonical homes by hand. Six governing documents mandate 1,449. This file is those 1,449 transcribed verbatim as atoms so the mapping act has a stable, citable subject: without it every re-reading of the documents produces a slightly different population and no disposition can be compared to the one before it.
$authoring: TRANSCRIPTION. Each label is the document's own wording. No atom is inferred, merged, split or renamed; repeats WITHIN one section are collapsed and repeats ACROSS sections are kept, because the same concept mandated twice is two mandates on one concept.
$not_a_requirement_register: These are MANDATES, not repository requirements. UAKOS-CLOSURE-009 owns the Repository Requirement Register and projects only concepts already in Repository Truth; its own posture forbids ingesting an external corpus ("CREATE = 0 at the concept layer"). Feeding these atoms there would breach the property that makes it trustworthy, so they live here, under the instrument that owns mandate mapping.

$section_kinds: Most sections mandate CONSTRUCTS -- things to build, reference or extend. Two do not, and the documents say so in their own headings. '016 STAKEHOLDERS' lists who the substrate serves; '017 TARGET DOMAINS' lists the markets it can be composed into. Treating either as a construct inverts the architecture: a target domain implemented as code is a FIXED INDUSTRY, which PRD principle P-001, LYR-NEG/LN-05 and MIP LAW P43-001 each forbid -- and 'industry' is a PROHIBITED_TOKEN the kernel refuses to seed. A register that dispositioned 'Agriculture' as CREATE would be instructing the repository to breach the mandate the same corpus states four sections earlier.
